text:
noah (AE): Heads-up: Nova Logistics requested a private VPC trial. Asking for 4 active nodes + 2 hot-standby. Asking 50% off platform fee month 1 and 60% off two active nodes for first 60 days.
tina (Sales Ops): Can you confirm standby topology? Hot-standby = reserved GPUs spun up and synced vs cold = deprovisioned? Billing differs.
lee (Solutions Eng): Hot-standby = reserved + warm KV cache. We can tag them as hot and meter separately. That still consumes capacity and counts toward reserved units.
noah (AE): They need instant failover for supply-chain spikes. Hot is required.
brooke (Deal Desk): We typically cap POC discounts so they don't exceed $5k ARR impact without exec sign-off. What's list pricing?
noah (AE): List: platform fee $5k/mo + 6 nodes * $2.5k = $15k -> $20k/mo. Proposed discounts = platform fee 50% off month1 ($2.5k) + 60% off 2 nodes (~$3k/mo for 2 nodes) for 2 months = ~ $6k total credits over POC.
omar (Finance): $6k credit okay if tied to conversion commitment. If they commit to a 9-month reserved contract for 6 nodes within 120 days, finance will approve. Otherwise cap credit to $4k.
lee (Solutions Eng): Tech note: KMS/HSM requirement: they want FIPS 140-2 HSM in EU region. That requires customer-provided HSM certs and schedule for integration. Could add a short onboarding services block (2 dev days).
legal-bot: Include security addendum template S-3 and updated DPA clauses for EU data residency. Legal will need completed security questionnaire and signed addendum prior to discount activation.
brooke (Deal Desk): Proposed compromise: Approve 40% discount on two active nodes for 60 days + platform fee waived month1. Contingent on signed POC addendum with conversion clause OR PO for services and HSM certs. RevOps must confirm SKU and proration.
kai (RevOps): We can create a one-off SKU: TRIAL-HOT-4A-2H with scheduled credits. Need deal desk approval email + copy of addendum to wire proration rules. ETA 48 hours to configure.
tina (Sales Ops): I'll draft the quote lines and the TRIAL SKU. Also will add optional line for 2 days of onboarding services ($6k one-time).
omar (Finance): If onboarding services billed separately and paid, we can stretch to $6k credit. Otherwise stick to $4k unless exec approves.
noah (AE): Customer also asked about SLAs for trial. Can we offer 99.5% with limited credit?
lee (Solutions Eng): For POC we can offer monitored SLA with an engineering on-call window, not full production SLA. That can be an addendum clause.
brooke (Deal Desk): Blockers before final sign-off: 1) legal completes addendum & DPA 2) RevOps confirms SKU + billing schedule 3) finance confirms final credit cap.
noah (AE): Timeline: Nova asked for final quote Tuesday COB. I'm on a call Monday. Need internal approvals before.
kai (RevOps): If deal desk posts approval by Monday morning and legal sends addendum by Monday EOD, we can have SKU ready by Tuesday morning.
legal-bot: Assigned to counsel Raj. ETA 2 business days barring redlines. If they need faster, we can use template S-3 with minimal edits.
brooke (Deal Desk): Action items: @lee draft technical addendum language (hot-standby definition + HSM notes), @tina draft quote with TRIAL SKU and onboarding line, @kai confirm invoice proration flow, @omar lock credit cap. If we get everything by Monday 10am, we can present to Nova same day.
noah (AE): I'll push them for a signed addendum and HSM certs on Monday call. Also will ask for a verbal commitment to convert within 120 days.
lee (Solutions Eng): Note: if they require full FIPS HSM managed by us we'll need partner approval; that adds 3-4 weeks and likely professional services. Flagging now.
tina (Sales Ops): Noted. I'll include both options in the quote: customer-managed HSM (no services) vs managed integration (PS fee).
brooke (Deal Desk): Tentative approval: 40% discount on selected nodes for 60 days + platform fee month1 waived, contingent on addendum + HSM certs + RevOps SKU. Final sign-off once legal & RevOps confirm. :white_check_mark:
noah (AE): Thanks team. Will report back after Monday call.
